forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. Two independent sources confirm operative rescission of the June 1 suspension before EOD June 16: (1) Araghchi confirmed at a June 16 press meeting with foreign ambassadors in Tehran that the MOU would be signed June 19 in Geneva, carried by IRNA and Tasnim — this is an official Iranian state-media statement that operationally supersedes the June 1 suspension within the resolution criteria's OR-branch (official MFA/state-media rescission); (2) The MOU framework text was digitally signed June 15 by named Iranian principal Ghalibaf and US principal Trump, with Pakistan as named mediator — a structured sign-off by named principals through a named mediator constitutes at minimum a partial qualifying event. Resolution: YES. Source corroboration: IRNA/Tasnim (June 16, via June 18 ToI liveblog), CNN June 12 (agreement close), Washington Post June 12 (Pakistan PM final text confirmed), NBC June 12 (Iran final deliberations).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both ways) occur in any 48h window before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE 0.55->0.20. No two-way direct Israel-Iran military exchange was confirmed within any 48h window between June 10 and June 19. The pre-window June 7-8 exchange (IDF strikes Iran, Iran launches ballistic missiles) does not count: it predates the June 10 resolution window start and cannot retroactively satisfy the criteria window (2026-06-10 to 2026-06-24). On June 14, IDF conducted strikes in the Beirut area; Iran prepared a response but US intervention — direct diplomatic communication to Iranian principals, per the Trump-Netanyahu call — caused Iran to stand down before executing a counter-strike. The June 14 event is therefore one-directional within the 48h window and resolves AMBIGUOUS-as-NO per the ambiguity rule ('one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO'). The Islamabad MOU signed June 17 establishes an immediate ceasefire across all fronts, reducing but not eliminating the probability of a qualifying two-way exchange in the remaining June 19-24 window. Probability set at 0.20 to reflect: ceasefire in effect, US actively managing Israeli-Iranian escalation, but Lebanon remains a latent flashpoint and 5 days remain within the window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Proxy-only attacks (Hezbollah/Houthi) without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do NOT count; one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE 0.20->0.08. The Islamabad MOU (June 17) commits Iran to reopen Hormuz immediately and the US to lift its naval blockade. First commercial movers — predominantly Chinese-flagged — began transiting June 17-18, with 18 transits recorded across that two-day window. PortWatch and AIS trackers recorded near-zero transits just days earlier (0 on June 14-16). CNBC (June 18) and NBC report industry experts project weeks to months for normalization: war-risk P&I insurance has not been reinstated, mine-clearing is ongoing (CENTCOM Operation Project Freedom launched May 4), and a vessel backlog has accumulated. Reaching a 7-day average of 50 transits/day by July 2 — within 13 days from effective MOU date — requires an acceleration rate not supported by any current AIS trajectory, insurer timeline, or expert projection.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
